overview.title: Biological Diversity Act 2002
overview.definition: A legislative framework enacted to provide for the conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising out of the use of biological resources and associated traditional knowledge.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Directly linked to GS Paper III (Environment & Ecology) and GS Paper II (Governance). Frequently tested due to its intersection with the Nagoya Protocol and IPR issues.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Biological Diversity Act 2002.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Objective**: To implement the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**, 1992, at the national level. 
• **Scope**: Covers biological resources, associated knowledge, and benefit-sharing. It applies to both Indian citizens and foreign nationals/entities. 
• **Institutional Structure**: A three-tier structure consisting of the **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)**, **State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs)**, and **Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)**. 
• **Key Metric**: The Act mandates **Prior Informed Consent (PIC)** and **Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT)** for accessing biological resources.

The mechanism ensuring that the benefits derived from the use of biological resources are shared with the local communities who conserved them.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **IPR Restriction**: No person can apply for any IPR (patent, etc.) based on biological resources from India without prior approval of the NBA. 
• **Heritage Sites**: The Act empowers State Governments to notify areas of biodiversity importance as 'Biodiversity Heritage Sites' (BHS).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Low awareness at the Panchayat level, delays in benefit-sharing fund disbursement, and conflict with the Patent Act. 
• **Solutions**: Digitalization of PBRs, capacity building for BMCs, and streamlining the ABS approval process.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: '3-Tier-ABS' 
• **Decoded Meaning**: 3-Tier (NBA-SBB-BMC), A (Access regulation), B (Benefit sharing), S (Sustainable use).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: The Act does not apply to 'cultivated crops' or 'value-added products' derived from biological resources. Many students wrongly assume it covers all agricultural produce.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Bio-piracy' when discussing the importance of the Act in protecting indigenous traditional knowledge from unauthorized patenting.

keyTakeaways: The Act is the primary legal instrument for fulfilling India's obligations under the CBD.
BMCs are the backbone of the Act, responsible for documenting local knowledge via PBRs.
The NBA is the final authority for granting approvals for IPRs related to biological resources.
